answer: Neighborhood Persistence Scoring. Each agent's score is the fraction of its graph neighbors that remain reachable through non-reciprocal edges over repeated epochs; a lone vertex on a sparse ledge scores near zero. Agents below a saffron threshold are excluded from matching and settlement. Creating a convincing neighborhood requires maintaining many distinct, long-lived links to unrelated agents, so each fake identity costs sustained relationship upkeep across epochs rather than a one-time fee.
